Kento Alpha 0.9.43, build 3125

New

  • Kento's assistant: an Assistant panel beside Properties, Shot and Feedback (Window > Panels > Assistant). Ask about the comp, or say what to change. It uses Kento's own tools, asks before each change (Apply or Skip), and makes a reply's changes one undo. It can run on this Mac (MLX LM, or an Ollama or LM Studio already running), on a machine in the studio, through an app you're signed into (Claude Code or Gemini CLI, no API key), or at a service with an API key (Anthropic, Google, OpenAI or another). Settings > AI and MCP > Kento's assistant sets it up.
  • The assistant can see the Viewer's picture (the + beside what it sees), use other apps' MCP servers such as Asobi's, and shows a card with Undo when another assistant changes the comp through MCP. A show can keep its comps away from remote services.
  • Nuke pre-renders come back as Reads: File > Import > Nuke pre-renders puts a Read of the frames in the node's place, keeps the node beside it turned off, and adds a note saying why. Right-click the Read and choose Use (the node) Again to go back.
  • Faster new frames at 4K: parts of a comp that are the same on every frame, such as a held frame or a still, are kept while you scrub, and TIFF, DPX and EXR files are read on all cores. On a heavy 4K comp a new frame went from about 1.3 s to 0.8 s, and a frame shown for the first time from 2.7 s to 1.6 s. Preferences > Performance's image cache is now shared with the render engine.
  • Kiri's Smart despill now follows the edge unmix: with edges unmixed, green is limited to the average of red and blue, and blue to the larger of red and green, the best on the studio's greenscreen tests.

Fixed

  • A transition saved as a Bento now plays in Nuke: its .nk had shown it finished on every frame.
  • Kiri's panel no longer shows its own bookkeeping (model folder, model id, model refresh, show) as rows to fill in: Kiri sets them itself.

Kento Alpha 0.9.42, build 3094

New

  • Kiri's CorridorKey edge route is finished. Renders, the render farm's included, now use CorridorKey's mattes as Kento's own render engine, as quickly as the rest of the comp.
  • Settings > AI and MCP > Kiri's edge model shows CorridorKey's install: what's downloaded and its size and licenses before anything starts, the progress with Cancel, Resume after a stop, and once installed Show the folder and Remove. Kiri's panel offers the same install.
  • Change the plate after working out a shot, and Kiri's model row says how many frames are out of date, so you know to work it out again.
  • 4K in tiles at full size: a choice on Kiri's model row for a frame bigger than 1536 x 1024. CorridorKey works on it in tiles at full resolution, feathered together, for finer detail (on a walking figure at 4K, 0.0004 from the true matte against 0.0005 fitted). It takes longer, and does worse on a subject close to the screen's color and on fine hair.

Kento Alpha 0.9.41, build 3089

New

  • Kiri's General edge route now works: CorridorKey 2.0, a matting model trained on screen keys, works out the shot's mattes in the background, and the frames it has done take its edge. It keys hair, motion blur and fine detail far closer than a key can: on a walking figure shot on green, its mattes came within 0.0006 of the true matte on average, where the key's own edge was 0.013 off. Press Install... on Kiri's edge row the first time (it downloads the model, about 3.7 GB, into Kento's own folder), then Work out the shot. Eight 2K frames take about 20 seconds. The mattes are saved beside the comp, so it renders anywhere without the model. CorridorKey 2.0's weights are under the Corridor Key Licence 2.0.
  • Settings > AI and MCP > Kiri's edge model: a Python and model folder for CorridorKey already on the Mac, used until Install has run.
  • Nodes with many inputs (three or more on one side, as Kiri has) now name their inputs only while you point at them, so the names no longer sit over their wires. Settings > Node Graph > Busy Nodes: Labels On Hover turns this off.

Fixes

  • Past a picture's edge, Keymix and Merge now read black or the edge pixels as Nuke does, channel by channel. A plate from a Read, a Crop or a Transform reads black past its edge until a node lifts its black (a Grade's add or lift, Invert, a Clamp's minimum, an Expression that isn't 0 on black). The Grain_Advanced gizmo now matches Nuke exactly, and L_Icolor is much closer. Write leaves a Read's black border out of the file only while every channel still reads black past the edge, as Nuke does.
  • A Transform with black outside on marks its picture black past its edge, as Nuke does.
  • Defocus still reads past a picture's edge its own way, which differs from Nuke's on a few pictures.
